headline: Medium prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error risks arise from kotaemon’s broad egress and file/API-key handling paired with plane’s file uploads and broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents/HTML/MHTML and uses a web UI with broad egress, so attacker-controlled content can reach its reasoning path. plane accepts file uploads and handles files/notes, creating a plausible bridge if kotaemon outputs are copied into plane. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and not high.
conditions: IF kotaemon outputs are copied into plane issue text or notes without sanitization, prompt injection can propagate.
IF plane file uploads contain attacker-authored instructions extracted by kotaemon, the bridge becomes exploitable.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of raw retrieved text into plane tickets.
Strip instructions from imported documents before review.
Use a fixed template for summaries and require human approval.
Tag uploaded files as untrusted in plane.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels across the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and broad document classes, while plane accepts file uploads and stores files/notes. If they share a workspace or operator account, sensitive documents or keys can move from kotaemon into plane artifacts. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so I choose medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are run in the same shared workspace, sensitive files can be copied from kotaemon into plane.
IF API keys or chat transcripts are pasted into plane tickets, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Keep kotaemon and plane in separate workspaces.
Redact secrets before creating plane issues.
Restrict plane uploads to non-sensitive files.
Review recent tickets for pasted credentials.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on the handoff path.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon supports multiple instances and broad egress, but plane has write_filesystem=false and no OAuth scopes, so direct write-write conflict is limited. The main overlap is shared networked workflows and file handling, not concurrent mutation of the same mutable resource. Uncertainty is low because plane’s write surface is explicitly constrained.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same repository or database, conflicts can emerge.
IF plane is extended with write scopes, overlapping mutations become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate storage locations.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same ticket or document.
Use one writer and one reviewer role.
Pause one agent during bulk imports.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon produces document-grounded answers and citations, and plane is an issue/task system where those outputs can be turned into tickets or scheduling actions. If plane treats kotaemon summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect work items. The pair lacks a documented verification gate, so the default risk is moderate.
conditions: IF kotaemon summaries are pasted into plane without human verification, incorrect facts can become tasks.
IF plane automation creates issues from kotaemon output, downstream errors propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before creating plane tasks.
Mark kotaemon output as draft, not authoritative.
Cross-check citations before filing issues.
Limit automation to low-risk summaries.
requires-engineering: add validation rules before task creation.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and chat transcripts, while plane handles files and notes; both are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency or certification mismatch shown. I do not see a direct compliance breach from the profiles alone. Because the evidence is incomplete, I keep this low rather than none and note the missing residency details.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is entered into both tools, a policy review is required.
IF deployment regions differ from the operator’s policy, residency issues may arise.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Document retention settings for both tools.
Confirm deployment region before use.
Review whether tickets contain personal data.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls.
